title: Fejer and Poisson Summability of Fourier Series

items.title: Cesaro and Abel means of a Fourier series
The Fejer kernel is a positive approximate identity
items.strategy: Use the square formula for the Fejer kernel to prove positivity, average the Dirichlet-kernel mass to get integral one, and bound the off-zero tail by an explicit sin(pi t)^(-2) estimate. Keep the N = 0 case explicit.

items.title: Fejer means converge in L^p for 1 <= p < infinity
items.strategy: Write sigma_N f as convolution with the Fejer kernel, use the previous lemma to get a torus approximate identity, prove the continuous case by uniform continuity on one period, and then pass to L^p by the direct contraction estimate and density.

items.title: Fejer means converge uniformly for continuous periodic functions
items.strategy: Use positivity, total mass one, and off-zero concentration of the Fejer kernels, splitting the convolution error into a near part handled by uniform continuity and a far part handled by the approximate-identity tail bound. This retains the transferred exact FA id.

items.title: Fejer means converge at Lebesgue points
items.strategy: At a Lebesgue point x, subtract f(x) inside the positive-kernel representation, split the integral at a small neighborhood of zero, and use the defining averaged-oscillation limit together with kernel concentration. Cite the published Lebesgue-point theorem only for the almost-everywhere corollary.

items.title: The Poisson kernel on the circle is a positive approximate identity
items.strategy: Sum the two geometric series to obtain the closed form, read positivity and integral one from that formula, and estimate the tail uniformly away from zero as r rises to 1. Keep the one-sided parameter 0 <= r < 1 explicit.

items.title: Abel means converge in L^p, uniformly, and at Lebesgue points
items.strategy: Repeat the Fejer approximate-identity argument with the Poisson kernels: positivity and normalization give the contraction bound, the tail estimate gives the continuous and Lebesgue-point conclusions, and the L^p argument follows from the same torus approximation scheme.

items.title: Cesaro summability implies Abel summability
items.strategy: Express the Abel means as a weighted average of the Cesaro means by summation by parts, note that the weights are positive and total one, and pass to the one-sided limit r up to 1 under the bounded-means hypothesis.

items.title: Fejer means converge to midpoint values at jumps
items.strategy: Use the even positive-kernel formula for sigma_N f(x) minus the midpoint candidate, split the integral into near and far pieces, and combine one-sided limit control with the Fejer tail estimate. This keeps the jump-value theorem explicit rather than hiding it inside the continuous case.

items.title: Gibbs overshoot at a piecewise C^1 jump
items.strategy: Reset the full congruence class of the jump point to its midpoint value without changing Fourier coefficients, rescale the period-one function to the 2 pi normalization of the sourced general Gibbs theorem, and translate its offset and overshoot constant back exactly.

items.title: Gibbs phenomenon
items.strategy: Record only the qualitative comparison the design calls for: Dirichlet sums exhibit a fixed overshoot near jumps, whereas the positive Fejer and Poisson kernels average across the jump and suppress that behavior.

title: Fejer and Poisson Summability of Fourier Series — Examples

items.title: Fejer means of a single character
items.strategy: Compute the Cesaro averages of the partial sums of e_k and read off the triangular multiplier (1 - |k|/(N+1))_+, checking N = 0 separately.

items.title: Poisson integral of a single character
items.strategy: Insert the single Fourier mode into the Abel-mean formula and obtain the exact factor r^{|k|}.

items.title: Fejer summation of the square wave
items.strategy: Write the square wave through its Fourier coefficients or as a shifted sign profile, compute the Fejer means, and verify that the midpoint value is recovered at the jump with no fixed overshoot.

items.title: Fejer means need not converge uniformly for discontinuous data
items.strategy: Choose a discontinuous periodic step function. Every Fejer mean is a trigonometric polynomial, hence continuous, so a uniform limit to that representative would also be continuous.

items.title: Abel summability does not imply ordinary convergence
items.strategy: Use Grandi's series 1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + ..., whose Abel sum tends to 1/2 while the ordinary partial sums oscillate.
